solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Medium strength?

blocks.note: surface reading: a middling degree of force, as in a medium-strength coffee or painkiller
setter's reading: the special power a spiritualist medium claims to have

explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' reads as an adjective meaning moderate; it is really a noun, the psychic who contacts the dead, and the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist medium's supposed gift is seeing beyond normal perception, which is exactly what this psychic faculty names.

clue.text: Response to standing ovation, one for The Archers?

blocks.note: first meaning read as two words: a performer takes an extended bow when the audience rises to applaud
second meaning: the tall English bow used by medieval bowmen

explanation.surface: A cast member of a radio soap takes their bows after a rapturous ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in a farming village, so the capitals pull you towards actors; here it just means people shooting arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The English longbow was the classic weapon of medieval bowmen, so it is a weapon suited to those who shoot arrows.

clue.text: Business run in Indiana (Springfield)

indicators.note: something put in another is enclosed by it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Indiana
Dusty Springfield was the British pop singer of the 1960s
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A company operates out of Springfield, a town in Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Springfield looks like the town, which makes Indiana feel natural; the bracketed name is really the singer Dusty Springfield, whose first name goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Business and commerce in general, the manufacturing and trading sector, is what this word means as a collective noun.

clue.text: Seductress undressed Evan, elected UK politician

indicators.note: to undress is to strip off the outer covering, so the outermost letters go and the inner ones stay

blocks.note: the name without its first and last letters
a Member of Parliament is elected to the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A femme fatale has stripped a newly elected politician called Evan.
explanation.walkthrough: MP stands for Member of Parliament, the elected representative in the UK House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a woman who uses her charms to seduce and exploit men, a femme fatale.

clue.text: Caution chicken about road?

blocks.note: yellow means cowardly, as does chicken
ca is short for circa, meaning about
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A warning to a chicken about crossing the road, echoing the old joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal, but it is simply CA, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee's formal caution to a player is shown by holding up this coloured card.

clue.text: “Vote against British!” — the French aristo

blocks.note: a vote against is a no
B is the abbreviation for British
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat urges people to vote against Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it sound like a slogan; really it is three short pieces strung together, the last borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristo is informal for aristocrat, and a nobleman or noblewoman is a member of the titled aristocracy.

clue.text: Idle traitor, boring, capricious

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so it ends up inside it

blocks.note: Eric Idle is the Monty Python comedian
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: A lazy, dull traitor who changes his mind on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' and 'boring' both pose as adjectives describing the traitor; Idle is the Python Eric, and boring means drilling into him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capricious acts unpredictably on sudden whims, and erratic likewise describes irregular, inconsistent behaviour.

clue.text: The headcount’s down to the bare bones

definitions.text: The headcount’s down to the bare bones

blocks.clueFragment: The headcount’s down to the bare bones
blocks.note: surface reading: a firm has cut its workforce to the absolute minimum
setter's reading: the workers who remain are only the bones of a body, a framework without flesh

explanation.surface: A company has cut its workforce as far as it can go.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare-bones idiom is taken literally: the minimum crew is pictured as a frame of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the minimum number of employees needed to keep an organisation running, like during holidays.

clue.text: Work on many scandals involving international tax shelter

indicators.note: to work on material is to rework and reshape it, so the letters are rearranged
to involve is to take in or include, so one piece is drawn inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Investigating a host of scandals about an offshore haven used by multinationals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International tax shelter' reads as one phrase, but 'international' supplies the I and only 'tax shelter' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This British overseas territory in the Caribbean levies no income or corporation tax, making it a famous offshore haven.

clue.text: Family dog barking madly first thing, in a state

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are jumbled
the first thing of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: kin are one's relatives
taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The family dog barks wildly first thing in the morning and gets everyone worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like an idiom for agitated; split it, and 'a state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a country or realm ruled by a monarch, so it is one kind of sovereign nation.

clue.text: Large peninsula country

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A big country sitting on a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large peninsula' reads as one phrase, but large only supplies its clothing-size letter and the peninsula follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African nation on the Atlantic coast, founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: Buffalo, Boston hosting Timberwolves

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the words hold the letters within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two city names

explanation.surface: Two American cities' teams entertain a basketball side, the Minnesota Timberwolves.
explanation.walkthrough: The cities and Timberwolves all suggest US sport; the answer sits across the end of Buffalo and the start of Boston.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobo is a Spanish-derived American word for the grey or timber wolf of the western United States.

clue.text: Second mother sat outside hospital dept (Labour wing)

indicators.note: sitting outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
mum is British for mother
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A second mother waits outside a hospital department in the Labour wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum is the left-wing campaigning group within Britain's Labour Party, not a hospital ward as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the grassroots organisation founded in 2015 to back Jeremy Corbyn, a faction inside the Labour Party.

clue.text: Land after flying over Dallas

indicators.note: things sent flying are scattered in all directions, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A plane touches down after flying over the Texan city of Dallas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a verb for an aircraft touching down; it is a noun, a country, and 'over' belongs to the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A land is a country or nation, and this is the smallest republic of Central America.

clue.text: Building support for Anne Boleyn finally?

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall residential or office building
second meaning read as two words: the executioner's block at the Tower of London, where Henry VIII's second wife died

explanation.surface: Building up support for Anne Boleyn, too late, as she finally faces execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' is not a last-letter signal: it means at the end of her life, when her neck was supported at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-rise block of flats or offices is a building; the second sense is a grim pun on the headsman's block.

clue.text: Closely examine Head of Chambers in hospital

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, its opening letter
something placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: the opening letter
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: A senior barrister in hospital gets a close medical examination.
explanation.walkthrough: Head of Chambers is a real title for the senior barrister of a set of lawyers' offices, which hides that only one letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan text or a scene is to look over it carefully, point by point, inspecting the detail.

clue.text: Hotly protesting bonkers puritanism banning bonking

indicators.note: to ban something is to keep it out, so those letters are removed
bonkers means crazy, so the letters are sent into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
'it' is a coy word for sex, which bonking is British slang for

explanation.surface: People furiously protest against a mad puritanical ban on sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonking is British slang for having sex, and 'it' is the usual crossword euphemism for the same thing; take those two letters out before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means indignant and vocally objecting, as if people had taken up weapons in protest.

clue.text: Bit on the side for Indian that swings both ways?

definitions.text: Bit on the side for Indian

indicators.note: something that goes either way reads the same whichever direction you take it

blocks.clueFragment: Bit on the side for Indian
blocks.note: a side order with a curry, whose four letters read the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A cheeky innuendo about a bisexual lover kept on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit on the side' and 'swings both ways' are slang for an affair and bisexuality; here they mean a side dish and a word reading the same both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: This flatbread is commonly ordered as an accompaniment to a curry in an Indian restaurant.

clue.text: Request jig, leaving daughter looking sceptically

indicators.note: when something leaves, it departs, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: to request is to ask
a jig is a lively dance
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter is asked to dance a jig and walks off, looking doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adverbial, describing how one looks at something, not a person doing the looking.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to regard something with suspicion or disapproval, eyeing it doubtfully.

clue.text: Cold day in spring, gasps in short trousers

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
the spring month, loosely indicated by a day falling in it
to pant is to gasp for breath

explanation.surface: On a chilly spring day someone gasps at the cold, wearing short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The month is clued loosely by 'day in spring', then trimmed by 'short'; the definition word 'trousers' sits beside the trimming signal, so it does double work in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri pants are close-fitting calf-length trousers, named after the Italian island resort where they became fashionable.

clue.text: Chant in support of old railway union, a caring profession

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the other

blocks.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, merged into the RMT in 1990
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: Workers chant in solidarity with a former rail union and a caring profession.
explanation.walkthrough: Chant comes first in the clue but sits last in the answer, because it is placed beneath the union in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing is the occupation of looking after the sick and injured, a profession built on patient care.

clue.text: Standard advice regarding daily fruit & veg portions?

definitions.text: advice regarding daily fruit & veg portions?

blocks.note: first meaning: the jazz standard by the Dave Brubeck Quartet

blocks.clueFragment: advice regarding daily fruit & veg portions?
blocks.note: second meaning read literally: the health campaign urging five portions a day

explanation.surface: The usual health advice about eating five servings of fruit and vegetables a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective for 'advice'; it is a noun, a well-known jazz tune, and the question mark flags the literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Dave Brubeck's 1959 recording is one of the best-known tunes in the jazz repertoire, a classic standard.

clue.text: Football’s wingers display talent

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so the letters at the two edges are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
to air something is to display it

explanation.surface: A team's wide players show off their skill on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Wingers are football players on the flanks, which disguises an instruction to take the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or stylish knack for doing something well, much like a gift.

clue.text: Work from Milan or Mantua?

indicators.note: something taken from a source is drawn out of it, so the letters come from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Is this piece of art from Milan or from Mantua?
explanation.walkthrough: Bellini's opera premiered at La Scala in Milan, so the surface question has a real answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A work is a piece of art or music, here Bellini's 1831 opera about a druid priestess.

clue.text: Leaders of all parties support Easter recess

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the one in front, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Political party leaders all back a break from Parliament over Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a parliamentary holiday; it is an architectural alcove, fitting Easter in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular vaulted alcove, usually at the east end of a church, a kind of architectural recess.

clue.text: Discovery Network is opening the country

indicators.note: an opening is a gap in the middle of something, so one piece sits in the middle of another

blocks.note: a find is a discovery
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: The Discovery TV channel is launching across a whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovery Network looks like the broadcaster's name; it is two separate pieces, with the computer network sitting in the middle of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Finland is a Nordic nation between Sweden and Russia, so it is a country.

clue.text: In flat, retailer regularly held raves

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper used to throw raves in their apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held' looks like the container signal, but it belongs with 'raves' in the definition; the opening 'In' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raves are big dance parties, so to have held raves is to have thrown parties and celebrated.

clue.text: Gutted Endeavour Morse rages over PC’s unhelpful response

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so only the outer letters remain
over can mean knocked over, upset, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: the first and last letters
taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Inspector Endeavour Morse, upset, rages at a police constable's unhelpful answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour Morse is the TV detective, so PC reads as police constable; it is really a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: When a personal computer fails it shows a notice reporting the fault, which rarely helps the user fix anything.
